for the fatal injuries sustained to Abhinav Jain in a road accident occurred on 05.01.2019.

"On 05.01.2019 deceased was travelling by car bearing no. DL-4CAU-2933 from Sohna Road TRP Hotel Gurugram to their residence with his friends and family.
When the abovesaid car reached at NH- 48 near Jharsa o the top of bridge, some voice came from behind of the car.

A truck which was coming from behind collided with right side of car.
Abhinav Jain who was sitting in right back seat of the car sustained injuries in this accident and died on spot.

The respondents have appeared and filed its reply.

In evidence, the petitioner examined two witnesses.
Smt. Akansha Jain was examined as PW1 and Sh. Mohit Goel was examined as PW2.

8. PW1 Smt. Akansha Jain deposed that on 05.01.2019 at 12.10 AM deponent, his husband Abhinav Jain was travelling by car no. DL-4CAU-2933 from sohna road TRP hotel Gurugram to their residence Delhi alongwith his friend Kunal Jain and his family.
When car reached at NH-48 near Jharsa, the top of bridge.
Car driver Kunal Jain take suddenly heavy break and stop the car to check the voice.
A truck which was coming from behind collided with right side of car.
Abhinav Jain who was sitting in right back set of the car sustained injuries in this accident and died on spot.
Right side of car also damaged in this accident.
This accident took place due to sudden taking heavy break on the bridge at NH-48 by the car driver.
Car driver was driving rashly, negligently and violating the rules of traffic.
Abhinav Jain was very intellectual and harworker and running his cloth business in Delhi.
Abhinav Jain earned Rs.5,00,000/- annually.

PW1 has relied upon the following documents:-

10. The respondent no. 3 examined as R3W1 Sh. Ankur Panchal who deposed that he is the associate employed with Smart Investigation Services who have been appointed by ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company to verify the details mentioned in the above claim petition.
He has brought the investigation report issued by Smart Investigation Services.
The said report comprises of the untrace report as well as the FIR with respect to the alleged accident.
The said report is Ex. R3W1/2 collectively.
As per their investigation, the accident took place due to the involvement of one Truck that fled from the place of accident.
In his cross-examination, he stated that he has no knowledge that the deceased was sitting in the car and one truck had hit the car.
11. I have heard the arguments as advanced by Ld. counsel for the parties and perused the record.

My issue-wise findings are as under :
ISSUE No.1 12.
It is well settled law that where petition under Section166 of the Act is instituted, it becomes the duty of the petitioner to establish rash and negligent driving by the driver.

In a petition under Motor Vehicles Act, Tribunal need not go into the Akansha Jain and ors. vs. Kunal Jain and Ors.. Page No.
6 of 9 technicality because strict rules of procedure and evidence are not followed.

sentences.text: Basically, in road accident cases, Tribunal has simply to quantify the compensation which is just rational and reasonable on the basis of enquiry.

Though it is an admitted legal position that the negligence on the part of driver with respect to the use of vehicle needs to be established but the same is to be established on the principles of preponderance of probabilities as decided in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Harsh Mishra & Ors. III(2015) ACC 435 Delhi.

sentences.text: Counsel for the insurance company had forcefully argued that no negligence can be attributed upon the respondent no. 1/ Kunal Jain because of the fact that the car was parked by the driver after coming to know some mechanical defect i.e. sound was coming and he has got down in the road side while in the process deceased who was sitting on the back rear side of the seat and got down from the right side, he was hit by the speeding truck as mentioned in the FIR.
Police had relied upon the statement of the respondent no. 1/Kunal Jain who had stated so and close the case as untraced.

Petitioner has not filed any protest petition even after coming to know that the case was closed and had not sought to implead the respondent no. 1 as the accused mentioning that it was the fault of the respondent no. 1 in the driving of the car rashly and negligently.
It is further submitted that no mechanical inspection report of the car has been brought before this Court so that damage can be ascertained.

Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the petitioner had stated that negligence was attributed to the Kunal Jain who was driving the said car and he had applied sudden brakes and in that process the truck which was coming from backside had hit the car and the deceased was succumbed to the injuries.
He submitted that protest petition could not have been filed because the claimant had suffered a lot and was undergoing in mental agony.

15. No doubt the burden of proving the negligence is upon the petitioners to prove that the respondent no. 1 was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently and had suddenly applied brakes so that the accident could have been happened.
However, no record has been brought herein to buttress this fact that the respondent no. 1 had applied brakes and car was hit by truck.
Car has not been taken into possession.

If the car has been hit by the offending truck then certainly car should have been damaged badly and not only the Abhinav Jain but 4-5 passengers sitting in the car would have been sustained injuries.
But here it is not the case as projected by the petitioners.
16. Moreover, in the present case, police had filed the closure report mentioning that the offending vehicle and its driver could not be traced.
There is no person including the petitioner and the respondent had made any statement attributed the negligence of the respondent no. 1 in causing the accident.
Akansha Jain and ors. vs. Kunal Jain and Ors..

entities.text: Akansha Jain and ors. vs. Kunal Jain and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page No. 8 of 9 17.
Ld. Counsel for the petitioner further had taken the plea that the petitioner was not in a mental condition but this fact is itself belied after perusing the record.
Claim petition has been filed by the petitioner for claiming the compensation for the death of his husband after one month and she had signed all the papers.
18. This fact shows that there was no negligence of the respondent no. 1 in causing accident.
Only some sound has been coming suddenly and he had stopped the vehicle and got down to see from where the sound has been coming.
It would be the deceased himself who would have got down from the right rear side of the car without seeing the traffic coming and in this process he would have been hit by the truck from behind.
19. These facts demonstrate that there was no negligence of the respondent no. 1 for causing the accident.

Therefore, the petitioner failed to prove that the respondent no. 1 was rash and negligent in driving the car bearing no. DL-4CAU-2933 of the alleged date time and place consequently deceased was died.
Therefore, this petition stands dismissed.
20. File be consigned to record room.
